title: Let --help reach a subcommand's help surface past the CLI-shape guard
action: In check_cli_shape (cli_shape.rs, the loop body around line 604), after parse_cli_flags produced `parsed` and BEFORE the validate() call, break out of the segment when `parsed.get("help").is_some()`. Rationale to carry in a short comment: --help is never a schema parameter in the registry (no "help" property exists in generated/registry_payload.json), so a parsed `help` key can only have come from the user asking for help; the CLI's own help surface answers it, and required-parameter validation must not stand in front of it. Test the PARSED key, not a raw token scan, so `--help` swallowed as another flag's value does not disarm the guard. Then add one #[test] to the module's test section next to a_segment_whose_shape_is_ambiguous_fails_open: allow("node .bee/bin/bee.mjs config set --help"), allow("node .bee/bin/bee.mjs config set --help --json"), and a deny("node .bee/bin/bee.mjs config set --key --help") asserting the reason still names config.set and the missing --value (there --help is consumed as --key's value, so no help key is parsed and the guard must still fire).

truths: `bee config set --help` and `bee config set --help --json` are allowed by the guard
A missing-required-parameter denial still fires when no --help was parsed
--help consumed as another flag's value does not disarm the guard
The full declared test suite is green

trace.outcome: check_cli_shape breaks out before validating when a help key was parsed, so bee <group> <cmd> --help reaches the CLI help surface
